plan.title: Paired within-subject treatment DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: Five subjects each contribute a control and a treated blood sample (paired design, 12000 genes x 10 samples, raw STAR/featureCounts integer counts). To find genes that respond to treatment within each subject, subject-to-subject baseline variation must be removed from the comparison rather than treated as noise, so the model blocks on subject and tests the condition (control vs treated) effect within that block. Step 1 profiles sample structure (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to confirm samples cluster by subject/pair as expected and to catch any mislabeled or outlier sample before fitting. Step 2 fits DESeq2 with design ~ subject + condition (explicit reference level = control), runs the paired Wald test for the condition coefficient, shrinks the log2 fold change with apeglm, and reports genes at BH-adjusted p < 0.05 with independent filtering — this is the direct answer to 'which genes respond to treatment within each subject'. Step 3 takes the full ranked gene list (Wald statistic) into fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (secondary) to surface coordinated pathway-level responses that individual gene-level significance may miss, respecting the human gene-set collections staged in the environment. Step 4 assembles the final report with both fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), the DE gene table (shrunken and unshrunken log2FC), the p-value histogram diagnostic, enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene-set collection versions, random seed).
